newsitem.title: USA: Koor sees $250 mln net income by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Koor sees $250 mln net income by 2000.

text.p: Israeli holding company Koor Industries Ltd said its board recently approved new business plans which would enable the company to post about $250 million in net income by the year 2000.

Koor's president and chief executive, Benjamin Gaon, said at a meeting in New York: "This focus should enable Koor to move beyond flat performance this year to revenues of $5 billion and net income of approximately $250 million by the year 2000."
In 1996, Koor posted revenues of $3.5 billion, net income of $180.8 million and earnings per American Depositary Share (ADS) of $2.39.
Gaon also said Koor's exports, which grew 11 percent to $1.2 billion in 1996, could more than double by the turn of the century, representing over 50 percent of its revenue.
Koor's core business were telecommunications and electronics, agrochemicals and building and infrastructure products.
Koor Chief Financial Officer Yehuda Milo said recent and planned divestitures of non-core businesses would yield capital gains of more than $100 million.
